exposure: uterine contraction shape (Fall to Rise ratio)
outcome: mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section due to lack of labor progress)
cohort: 200 primiparous women with a single, cephalic presentation pregnancy.
finding: A higher uterine contraction Fall to Rise (F:R) ratio and lower contraction frequency were significantly associated with a lack of labor progress.
mod_finding: The average F:R ratio was significantly higher in the cesarean section group (1.64) compared to the vaginal delivery group (1.13), and contraction frequency was lower in the cesarean section group.
cross-section timing: At the beginning of the active phase of labor (dilatation 3-5 cm) for 30 minutes.
